Forgot one? Hold FN on its own for a moment, in any app or game, and this list shows up. Let go of FN to close it.
Your games
Games go on the EASYROMS partition of the SD card. In a computer, the card shows up as a drive called EASYROMS. On the console, it\'s the EASYROMS storage in the Files app.
Give every system its own folder, named like nes, snes, gb, gba, megadrive or psx. Cards set up for ArkOS or dArkOS already use these names, so their games work as they are.
The console makes these folders on EASYROMS by itself, with a README listing which system goes where.

No computer or card reader at hand? Open Wi-Fi transfer on the console and scan its QR code with your phone, or type the address it shows into any browser on the same network, to send games straight to EASYROMS.
Daijishou, the home screen, turns those folders into a game library: add a platform and pick its folder on EASYROMS.
Emulators

RetroArch and PPSSPP come preinstalled. RetroArch already has the cores for NES, SNES, Game Boy, GBA, Mega Drive, Master System, Game Gear, PlayStation, PC Engine, Neo Geo Pocket, WonderSwan, Atari 2600, 7800 and Lynx.
PSP games run in PPSSPP. PlayStation games start without a BIOS, but work best with one in the bios folder on EASYROMS.
The emulators are ordinary apps: F-Droid can update them, and you can uninstall them.
Speed and battery

Settings > Performance has three profiles. Battery saver for long sessions with older systems, Balanced for everyday use, Performance for PS1, N64 and PSP. The Quick Settings tile switches between them too.
Settings > CPU overclock (experimental) runs the processor faster than standard for demanding games. A restart turns it off. If the console freezes, pick a lower speed.
CPU overclock (experimental), on the same page, runs the processor faster than standard for demanding games. A restart turns it off. If the console freezes, pick a lower speed.
The screen uses the most power. Lower brightness means longer play time.
Mouse and buttons
Hold both sticks pressed in for a second: joystick mouse on or off
Move the pointer
Click, hold R1 to drag
Right click
Scroll
Settings > Joystick mouse changes speed, buttons and the combination.
Settings > Button mapping swaps buttons, with profiles for different games.
Locked yourself out? Hold both volume buttons for 5 seconds and every button is back to normal.
Going online

Most R36S consoles have no Wi-Fi built in, but some models, such as the R36XX, do. If yours has it, just turn on Wi-Fi in Settings > Network & internet. If not, plug a USB Wi-Fi adapter into the OTG port, with a USB-C adapter if it needs one, then turn on Wi-Fi there.
Cromite is the web browser.
Troubleshooting
Most problems can be fixed with a computer and the SD card. On a computer, the card shows a small drive called BOOT (the start files) and a big one called EASYROMS (your games).
The first start takes a long time
That\'s normal. The first start sets up the SD card and restarts on its own, then Android prepares its apps. Give it a few minutes and don\'t switch it off.
The screen stays black on the first start, but the console is on

Your console has a different screen than the one this card was set up for. On a computer, open BOOT, then Panels. Copy both files from one of the Panel folders to the top of BOOT and replace the files there. Panel4 is the default, so try the others one at a time.
It stopped starting after an update or a Magisk module

Start it without root. On a computer, open BOOT and rename ramdisk.uimg to ramdisk-magisk.uimg, then rename ramdisk-stock.uimg to ramdisk.uimg. Your apps and games stay. Rename them back later to get root again.
The console froze
Hold Power for about 10 seconds until it switches off, then switch it on again. If it froze with the CPU overclock on, pick a lower speed next time. A restart always turns the overclock off.
A game doesn\'t start, or starts to a black screen

Some systems, like Sega CD and PC Engine CD, need a file from the original console (a BIOS), and PlayStation games work better with one. Put these files in the bios folder on EASYROMS. Settings > Emulator files shows what\'s missing.
The buttons do the wrong thing
Recovery and factory reset
Hold FN while you switch the console on
This starts the recovery system, used for a factory reset or to install updates from a computer. A factory reset erases your apps and settings, but not the games on EASYROMS.
The date or time is wrong
The console forgets the time when the battery runs completely empty. Set it in Settings > System > Date & time. With a network connection it sets itself, as long as "Use network-provided time" is on.
USB and computers
The easiest way to copy games is to put the SD card into a computer and copy them to EASYROMS. Put the card back before you switch the console on.
Connect the console to a computer

Turn on Settings > USB mode > Connect to a computer, then plug a data cable into the OTG port and a USB-A port on the computer. Pick File transfer in the USB notification. Pads and adapters on the OTG port don\'t work while this is on, and a restart turns it off.

Never turn this on if your console has Wi-Fi built in, such as the R36XX. Those consoles use this same USB port for their Wi-Fi, so Wi-Fi stops working and may not come back until you restart. USB mode asks before it switches.
Never use this while the console is charging from its other port. Unplug the charger first. If a charger is plugged in while it is on, USB mode switches back to accessories.
For adb, also turn on USB debugging in Settings > System > Developer options. To show Developer options, click Build number 7 times in Settings > About console.
The OTG port is for accessories: pads, USB drives and network adapters. It can\'t connect to a computer on this build.
Accessories

Plug accessories into the OTG port, with a USB-C adapter or a small hub if needed. USB pads, keyboards, mice, USB drives, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and Ethernet adapters work if Android has a driver for their chip. Adapters with common Realtek chips work best. On consoles with Wi-Fi built in, such as the R36XX, something plugged into the OTG port can stop the built-in Wi-Fi.
Nothing happens? Unplug it, wait a few seconds and plug it in again. Some adapters need more power than the port gives; a hub with its own power supply helps.
SD card
The card holds everything: Android, your apps and data (16 GB), and EASYROMS, which gets the rest of the card. EASYROMS uses exFAT, so Windows, macOS and Linux can all read it.
All the space for apps, no EASYROMS

Before the very first start, make an empty file named .noroms on BOOT. The first start then gives the whole card to apps. This only works on a freshly written card. BIOS files then go in the bios folder on the internal storage.
Back up your saves

Saves made next to the games on EASYROMS are easy to copy on a computer. Saves inside an app stay with that app on the Android part of the card, so check each emulator\'s settings for where it keeps them.
Battery care
The battery percentage looks wrong

The battery gauge guesses the charge and learns as it goes. After the battery ran empty or the console sat unused for a long time, charge it to 100% with the console on and leave it on the charger for another half hour. That lets the gauge find the right level again.
Settings > Battery > Battery details shows the battery voltage: about 4.2 V is full, below 3.5 V is nearly empty.
Sleep or power off?
Sleep (tap Power) is fine for breaks, but still uses a little battery. For more than a day, power it off from the power menu.
Putting it away for a while
Charge it to about half and power it off. Top it up every few months. A battery left completely empty for a long time can wear out.
Root (Magisk)
The console comes with root through Magisk. Apps that ask for root show a prompt: allow or deny it with the buttons. The Magisk app manages root access and modules.
Root lives on the BOOT part of the card, so it stays when the system is updated.
A module broke the start
See Troubleshooting: on BOOT, swap ramdisk.uimg for ramdisk-stock.uimg, and the console starts without root and modules.
